scope: Kept the same async lifecycle decisions and correct option IDs. Reworked the three wrong alternatives in each object into case-specific competing contracts and rebound their messages; no array reordering, external delivery guarantee, or rollback promise was added.

items.learningObjective: Distinguish cancellation of waiting from operation ownership, commit state, and cleanup obligations in the stated async case.
items.decisiveFact: In A package-label generation service, A print job can be shared by two callers. If one caller cancels its wait, the other still needs the same approved shipment revision rendered; the shared job must release its temporary file on completion. Which async-operation contract should the owner expose?
items.nearestAlternative: Cancel the shared render when any caller cancels, even while another caller still needs it.
items.identityReason: The accepted lifecycle boundary and owner_preserves_contract decision remain the same; only competing policy meanings were rewritten and therefore receive fresh option IDs.
sourceRefs: Fictional async operation and commit facts are explicit in the prompt; no exactly-once or rollback guarantee added.
